Keep the gradient from the best-scoring run and change only temperature to test selectivity of its unresolved pair. The higher temperature should shorten retention, preserving the sub-10-minute elution window while potentially improving the critical separation.

Return to the best run’s temperature and solvent endpoints, changing only gradient duration to measure the critical pair’s slope sensitivity. This substantially steeper gradient should retain the time advantage and reveal whether compression improves selectivity or worsens the unresolved pair.

Shift the solvent window lower while preserving injection 10’s gradient slope to test solvent-dependent selectivity of the remaining unresolved pair. Its 6.03-minute last peak leaves room for increased retention without immediately incurring a time penalty.

Lower the solvent window another step while preserving the slope and temperature that produced CRF 0.981, aiming to bring the remaining critical pair to R ≥ 1.5. The last peak is expected near 10 minutes, so this tests the resolution gain close to the time-penalty boundary.

Injection 12 reached the maximum CRF with resolution margin for every pair. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to reduce elution time while testing whether full resolution and CRF 1.000 can be preserved.

Use a gradient slope between injections 12 and 13 by lowering phi1 one step. This should recover R ≥ 1.5 for the critical pair while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes, potentially preserving maximum CRF with a shorter separation.

Raise temperature one grid step from injection 14 to seek a shorter fully resolved separation. Holding the gradient fixed isolates temperature selectivity, with particular attention to the pairs currently at R 1.73 and 1.89.

Return to 25 C and raise phi0 one step from injection 14 to shorten retention while making the gradient shallower. Relative to injection 11, the reduced slope may bring its R 1.31 pair above 1.5 while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a narrower gradient window to seek a faster fully resolved separation. The shallower slope is intended to offset the critical-pair resolution lost when phi0 increases, while injection 16 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Shorten injection 17’s gradient by one grid step to test the speed limit at this solvent window. The critical pair has only modest resolution margin, so retain injection 17 as the confirmed maximum-score fallback if its resolution drops below 1.5.

Test a modest temperature increase with a slope between injections 17 and 18, aiming to recover critical-pair selectivity while shortening retention. The larger early-pair separation at this starting composition may tolerate warming better than injection 15 did.

Lower phi1 one step from injection 19 to make the gradient shallower and improve its remaining unresolved pair. This also isolates the temperature effect relative to fully resolved injection 17, seeking maximum CRF with a last peak earlier than 8.99 minutes.

Return to 25 C and use a slope between injections 11 and 16, slightly steeper than the fully resolved injection 16. This targets a last peak just under 9 minutes while retaining R ≥ 1.5; the longer programmed gradient provides finer slope adjustment on the allowed grid.

Test whether 35 C moves the close pairs past the selectivity crossings seen at 30 C, using injection 16’s fully resolved gradient as the reference. This seeks a substantially faster maximum-score method while retaining injection 21 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved option.

Preserve injection 20’s initial gradient slope but transition to the hold after the early critical peaks elute. The hold tests a change in late-pair selectivity to resolve its sole remaining deficient pair while targeting a last peak below 10 minutes.

Increase temperature one step from injection 22 to test whether its near-coeluting pair separates after an elution-order crossing. All other pairs were resolved at 35 C, so this offers a chance of a faster maximum-score separation while retaining injection 21 as the confirmed fallback.

Use a slightly steeper slope than fully resolved injection 17, targeting R near 1.5 and a last peak slightly earlier than injection 21’s 8.90 minutes. The longer programmed gradient enables fine slope adjustment on the grid; all peaks should elute well before its endpoint.
